session_summary: Implemented full automation for keeping the GitHub Pages site and README in sync with the guides/ directory. Four tasks completed across three phases: (1) made docs/index.html dynamic using manifest.json, (2) extended gen_manifest.py to regenerate README Guides table, (3) added a CI commit-back step to deploy-pages.yml, (4) created scripts/sync-docs.sh and updated CLAUDE.md rules. All tasks completed successfully on first try with no retries needed.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Handled vanilla HTML/JS editing cleanly despite the template being oriented toward React/TypeScript. Correctly followed the existing fetch-from-manifest pattern in docs/guides/index.html. Python script extension was clean and accurate.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: The agent's template emphasizes React components and Express routes heavily, but this session required vanilla JS and Python scripting. The agent adapted fine but the template framing could note it handles vanilla HTML/JS tasks too.
agent_feedback.suggested_change: Add a note in the responsibilities section: also handles vanilla JS scripting, static HTML pages, and Python utility scripts when the project context requires it.

agent_feedback.worked_well: Correctly identified that contents: write permission was needed in the workflow to push the README commit back. The [skip ci] pattern was used correctly. sync-docs.sh was well-structured with proper guards.
agent_feedback.needs_improvement: No significant gaps. The agent proactively caught the missing permissions: contents: write without being prompted.

overall_notes: Parallel execution worked well throughout. Tasks 1 and 2 ran simultaneously with no file conflicts (different files). Tasks 3 and 4 also ran in parallel with no conflicts. Total of 4 agents invoked across 2 parallel batches. The investigation phase (reading 8+ files before planning) was essential — it revealed that docs/guides/index.html was already dynamic and only docs/index.html and README.md were broken. Without that investigation, a solution might have over-engineered the already-working parts.
